summary: Proceed only once the binding is known to take the kwargs. Get that answer for free by putting an untimed print-only signature probe and config sweep table into prepare() of the next moe run already being dispatched. Spending a check to learn 'kwargs absent' or 'nothing beat 3%' just re-measures master, which was measured an hour ago (a2744bc496b84790, 1.3445x). Before building, raise the adoption margin from 3% to at least 8% (with two routings) and measure correctness against fp32, because the LESSONS cuBLASLt dead knob mostly transfers.
justification: Where the time goes is real. On master (a2744bc496b84790) bs=8/16/32 run at 106.0/147.7/198.7 us against floors of 37.3/52.5/70.8 us, roughly 35% of the 4.8 TB/s floor. Marlin is 92-96% of each shape. bs=32 is the weakest load at 1.034x vs SGLang. The mechanism as written is weak on three counts. (1) The arithmetic is off. I = H = 4096, so w13 has N = 8192, which is 64 n-tiles at Marlin's default thread_n = 128, not 32. More importantly, Marlin's striped partition spreads the (m-block x n-tile x k-tile) space evenly over the persistent CTAs precisely to avoid wave quantization. A different tile changes slice count, reduction depth and bytes in flight per CTA, not wave fill. (2) The candidate grid partly duplicates the default. For thread_m_blocks = 1 (block_size_m 8, and 16 at T=32), Marlin's small-batch list is (128,128,256 thr), (64,128), (128,64), and the heuristic takes the first valid one, so (128,128) is very likely the default under another name. (64,256) is a large-batch config that may be invalid or not instantiated at small M, so it would raise. In practice the sweep is (64,128) and (128,64) times blocks_per_sm in {1, 2}. blocks_per_sm = 1 or 2 means fewer CTAs, which means fewer bytes in flight. That usually hurts a bandwidth-bound small-M GEMV, the opposite of the hope. (3) Local priors are against it. Every mid-M Marlin knob tried here was flat: marlin-workspace-blocks-per-sm-8, w13 atomic add, w13 bf16 reduce, and the two-stream halves. Only block_size_m (at M >= 128) and w2 atomic add (bs=1, by removing a slow mode) moved anything. Expected direction and size: a 5% win at one shape is about +0.8% geomean, inside the ±1.5% headline CI but visible in that shape's paired ratio (err ~2 us, ~1.5%). The expected rows cite 'Marlin pair ~170 us' at bs=16 and '156-207' at bs=32. Those come from single-profile rows that are noisy: this very job shows Marlin 121.5 us at bs=32 but 176.6 us at bs=16, with profile totals 131.6 vs 184.7 us against judged 198.7 vs 147.7. Read the paired ratios, not the profile. On the LESSONS cuBLASLt transfer question, most of it transfers. bf16-cublaslt-algo-pick-in-prepare picked a config that was 6.8% faster in prepare and became 14% slower in the judge, about a 20-point swing. Prepare timings also undercount the judge by 20-25%. A 3% margin sits deep inside that swing, so the selector would mostly be choosing on noise. Two things make Marlin somewhat less hopeless than cuBLASLt. Cold-L2, graph-replay, interleaved timing is closer to the judge than the bf16 pick was. And these candidates differ structurally (CTA count, tile), so a real effect would be large, not a near-tie. That argues for a much higher bar, not for dropping the idea. Requirements: margin >= 8%; the win must reproduce on two synthetic skewed routings (different seeds, sized to the judge's 7-13 touched experts at the right per-expert counts) and in two interleaved passes; the pair (w13 + act + w2) is timed as one graph in the exact master mode; the sorted per-config table is printed and the winner asserted (LESSONS 03:41Z). Weakest link: there is no evidence that SGLang's moe_wna16_marlin_gemm (sglang.kernels.ops.moe, the b_bias-era signature) exposes thread_k/thread_n/blocks_per_sm at all. No local SGLang is installed and no archived log prints its version or signature. The vLLM-lineage kernel hard-codes -1 internally in several versions.
confounders: w2-marlin-atomic-add-small-m (9080a71): w2 at T<=32 runs use_atomic_add=True with use_fp32_reduce=True (log: PATH CHOSEN = atomic, worst rel-L2 0.00479 vs master). thread_k and blocks_per_sm change the k-slice count, so they change both the atomic chain cost and its bf16 rounding. The w2 sweep must run in master's w2_mode, not the default flags, or the ranking is of a different kernel. The proposed 5e-3 rel-L2 bound against the default config is barely above atomic's own 4.79e-3 jitter, so it will reject valid configs at random. Bound against an fp32 reference at master's own error plus a margin instead.

marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm / triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack: these fix block_size_m (8 at T<=16, 16 at T=32), which sets thread_m_blocks and therefore which (thread_k, thread_n) are valid. The sweep must use master's per-T block_size_m. The queued marlin-two-class-block-m-decode32 would change bs=32's block size and make a T=32 pick stale, so do not stack the two without re-sweeping.

sglang-marlin-path-parity: the lock workspace comes from marlin_make_workspace(max_blocks_per_sm=4). Candidates of 1 and 2 stay inside it, so this is not a confounder for the proposed grid. Never sweep above 4 without a matching workspace (marlin-workspace-blocks-per-sm-8 already showed the workspace itself is neutral).
align and post-norm landings (align-parallel-per-expert-verify, post-expert-norm-triton-small-m): they share no launches or traffic with the Marlin config, so they do not confound.
interference: No companion. The change is gated to bs=8/16/32, so bs=1/128/256 run byte-identical master launches as in-run controls, and the printed PATH CHOSEN table names exactly which (kernel, T) changed. A gain or loss on a changed shape is attributable without an ab-revert. Reverting the w2 atomic add would measure a kernel nobody ships, and an ab-tune of block_size_m belongs to marlin-two-class-block-m-decode32. The real waste is the no-op outcome, not ambiguity. If the binding lacks the kwargs, or no config clears the margin, the check re-measures master, which a2744bc496b84790 measured an hour ago. The 'master control' framing does not justify that spend: drift in this harness is already recorded (untouched rows move 2-6% between batches), and a duplicate master run adds nothing the board does not have. Mitigation, in order: (a) an untimed, print-only probe goes into the next moe run being dispatched anyway (e.g. swapab-w13-silu-epilogue-verify, queued on master). The probe does a try/except kwargs call of moe_wna16_marlin_gemm with thread_k/thread_n/blocks_per_sm on dummy inputs, prints the signature or TypeError, and prints the sorted cold-L2 sweep table. It applies nothing. (b) Mint this hypothesis for dispatch only if that table shows a config >= 8% faster at some (kernel, T) on both routings. Otherwise retire it as a dead knob with the table as evidence. If the churn cannot piggyback, run it as an okc check (never a submit) and record a kwargs-absent outcome as 'knob unavailable', not 'neutral'.
rules_flags: No rule problem in principle. The config is chosen in prepare() and stored as Python ints keyed by num_tokens (a shape), and kernel_fn branches only on shape, with no host sync and no values derived from data.

Spec gap: 'by T' at 8 <= T <= 32 but tuned only at T = 8, 16, 32. Apply stored configs only at exactly those T and keep the default elsewhere, including any T in 9..31. A T=33 test or bs=4 test must never see a tuned config (they are outside the range; keep it so).

Use inspect.signature only as a hint. A pybind or torch.ops builtin may have no signature, or the Python wrapper may take **kwargs. Decide availability with a guarded trial call on dummy inputs in prepare, and print the result. An invalid config raises a TORCH_CHECK (recoverable), not a device fault, so try/except is safe here, unlike the 715 case in LESSONS.

Print compactly and late: archived logs are a ~15 KB tail. The PATH CHOSEN table must survive, with one line per (kernel, T) giving default p50, best p50 and the chosen config, plus an assert that the chosen config is the printed winner.
open_questions: Does the judge image's sglang.kernels.ops.moe.moe_wna16_marlin_gemm accept thread_k/thread_n/blocks_per_sm? A zero-cost piggyback print answers it before any check is spent.

Which exec config does Marlin's heuristic pick at moe_block_size 8 and 16 for N=8192/K=4096 (w13) and N=4096/K=4096 (w2)? If it is (128,128) everywhere, half the proposed grid is the default under another name.

Is Marlin at mid-M limited by tile config at all, or by block_size_m padding and per-expert weight re-reads (bs=16 with block 8 splits popular experts into several m-blocks that each stream that expert's weights)? If the latter, marlin-two-class-block-m-decode32 is the right lever and this knob will be flat.
Should the adoption margin be calibrated from data? Running one config against itself twice in prepare gives the noise floor; the winner then has to beat the default by max(8%, 3x that floor).
